findings.title: Spec expects TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job
findings.body: In the test environment queue_jobs is false, so `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic)` runs the job inline. That job calls `TopicRetriever.new(url, no_throttle: ...)` and the stub returns a bare mock. The spec only works through this indirect path. It does not check that the job is enqueued with the right args.

findings.title: Referer interpolated unescaped into inline JS
findings.body: Line 11 writes `request.referer` into a JS string literal with `<%= %>`. That helper HTML-escapes but does not JS-escape, so a backslash or other JS-significant character in an attacker-chosen referer can break out of the literal. The host check only validates the host part, and the path and query of the referer are still attacker-controlled. The target origin should be built from the configured embeddable_host instead.

findings.title: Unescaped URL injected into raw HTML post
findings.body: The feed or remote URL is interpolated directly into `<a href='#{url}'>` without escaping. Posts using cook_method raw_html skip sanitization, so a URL containing `'` or `<` produces stored XSS. Imported feed content as a whole is also rendered with `raw post.cooked` and never sanitized, so a compromised feed source can inject scripts.

findings.title: Mutates caller's string; fails on frozen strings
findings.body: `contents <<` modifies the argument in place. Callers passing literals or frozen strings, such as `doc.content`, may get errors. The caller's data is also silently altered.

findings.title: open(url) with untrusted input allows command execution/SSRF
findings.body: Kernel#open from open-uri is called on the URL. A value starting with '|' executes a shell command. The disqus import passes thread links straight from the XML file, and the URL is not validated as http before this call. Use URI.parse(url).open or an HTTP client, and validate the scheme first.

findings.title: Race creating duplicate embeds
findings.body: Two concurrent imports of the same URL can both see no existing embed. Both then create a topic, and the second `TopicEmbed.create!` raises on the unique index. Because creator.create runs inside the transaction, this rolls back with an exception that is not handled.

findings.title: Nil content crashes feed poll
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError for RSS items that have no content (only a description), which aborts the whole poll. `scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1.

findings.title: Every embed miss triggers a full feed poll
findings.body: Each retrieve for an unknown URL synchronously polls and imports the entire feed. Staff requests bypass throttling, so this can cause repeated heavy fetches.

findings.title: Start discussion branch unreachable
findings.body: @topic_view is only set when a topic exists, and that topic always has at least the imported post. The 'start_discussion' branch therefore never shows, even when a topic has no replies.
